The incident took place in a Project Area. During execution of electrical cable laying activity by the contract workman (hereinafter called Injured Person (IP)), the fall incident occurred at the junction point of East-West to North-South pipe rack. IP was working with proper personal protective equipment including a full body safety harness anchored to a secure point. Subsequently, he moved towards the North-South pipe rack through the horizontal portion of the cable tray to perform cable dressing activity. The cable tray arrangement consisted of three layers, and the workman was moving with his feet on the lowest cable tray while holding the top layer cable tray with his hands for support. During the movement he had not anchored the full body safety harness. When the workman inadvertently held a loose overhead cable tray, he lost his balance and fell. The loose cable tray got stuck on the beam, while the workman fell approximately 2.8 meters to the ground level. He initially appeared unharmed and was conscious. He was immediately shifted to the Occupational Health Centre, where first aid was administered. Subsequently, he was referred to a hospital and later shifted to a higher medical facility for further treatment. Unfortunately, the injured workman succumbed during treatment around 16 days later. OBSERVATIONS / LAPSES
1. The IP was wearing personal protective equipment; however, the full body safety harness was not anchored during movement at height.
2. Proper walkway/ scaffolding had not been constructed for the job.
3. Illumination at the work site was not adequate.
4. Proper supervision was not done by the job supervisor during execution of the critical activity. CONCLUSION/ ROOT CAUSE
1. Non-anchoring of safety harness during movement at height, indicating unsafe work practice and inadequate supervision.
2. Absence of proper scaffolding/ walkway for work at height. This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents. Line of fall (2.8 meter)

context.title: Fatal Fall from Height during Electrical Cable Laying Activity
context.corrective_actions:
1. Work at heights shall be carried out on properly erected and inspected scaffolding platforms. Scaffolding with adequate platforms, handrails, and all stipulated appurtenances shall be provided at all such locations in line with OISD-GDN-192.
2. Possibility of using secondary protection devices such as safety net or fall arrestor should be explored for execution of such jobs.
3. Adequate illumination should be available at work site, particularly where work at height is being carried out. ************ This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents.

text:
A 14" carbon steel pipe spool piece (approx. 6 m long, 700 kg) was being lifted using an EOT crane at the UFRO shed of the RODM plant construction site by team of contract personnel. During the lift, the crane's pendant control panel malfunctioned, and the limit switch failed resulting in uncontrolled upward movement of pipe. This led to the web slings being pulled against the EOT girder, where they sheared, causing the pipe spool piece to fall. The spool bounced and struck a rigger standing beneath the structural platform. The injured rigger was taken to hospital where he later succumbed to his injuries. OBSERVATIONS/ LAPSES
a) The pipe spool was to be lifted and placed on a platform/ structure (almost in the east side portion of the shed) at a height of about 5 M.
b) An EOT crane, recently commissioned (4 days before the incident), was being used for the lifting and erection activity. As per MOM (installation and commissioning of EOT), following operational checks were performed:
• Main hoist operation with limit switch with auto cut
• Cross travel operation with limit switch with auto cut
• Long travel operation with limit switch with auto cut Functioning of emergency stop button was not recorded in MOM.
c) A lifting team, consisting of 2 riggers and 1 operator, assembled at the site for the task. Supervisor (Engineer) of contractor was also present at site.
d) The riggers positioned the pipe for lifting and installed two web slings, each rated for 3 MT capacity, around the pipe.
e) Guide ropes were fixed on both ends of the pipe to control its horizontal movement during lifting.
f) After receiving signal from the riggers, the crane operator started lifting the pipe vertically using the pendant type control panel of hoist system. This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents.
g) During the lifting (hoisting) of the pipe spool piece, the vertical-up movement button on the EOT crane pendant panel got stuck. The operator attempted to stop the upward hoisting by tapping and releasing the button, but it remained engaged. As a result, the hoist and pulley moved past the bridge-girder level where they were supposed to stop.
h) The Limit Switch also did not function, and the upward movement of the pipe went out of control of the operator. The operator also tried to engage the emergency stop button on the pendant but that also did not work.
i) Initially one web sling, holding the pipe, came into contact with the edge of the girder and sheared/tore due to tension. The second web sling also failed subsequently, compromising the stability of the load. The pipe got detached and fell from height of about 6M onto the ground.
j) The pipe spool piece fell on the ground and apparently bounced and hit one of the riggers on his lower body near knee level. Though the rigger was standing under a nearby structural platform, which was found otherwise safe, the pipe spool while bouncing intruded/entered about 1.5M inside the platform (towards south side) and hit the Rigger.
k) The injured rigger was assisted, and emergency response actions were initiated. He was taken to hospital where he later succumbed to his injuries.
l) The stuck "UP' button in the pendant panel, malfunctioning of limit switch probably due to contact failure/ control-contactor/ wiring related issue, and failure of emergency push button indicated improper inspection and questionable reliability/ workmanship of the EOT.
m) No record of pre-job EOT check was evident. CONCLUSION/ ROOT CAUSE Inadequate/ improper inspection/ questionable reliability/ workmanship of the various safety provisions (limit switch, emergency stop, etc.) of the EOT.

text:
Welding job of supports for newly erected bypass line to eccentric orifice downstream of crude oil separator was being carried out in morning shift. At around 15 minutes before noon, contract personnel noticed fire in the adjacent storm water channel. They tried to extinguish the same with portable fire extinguishers. A company employee passing by the area noticed the fire and informed control room, which in turn informed the sub fire station. Contract personnel along with company operating staff laid firewater hose and started applying water in channel through fire hydrants. Fire spread through storm water channel to De-emulsifier drums in east, and to cables and junction boxes in north-west, both approximately 50-60 meters apart. Fire team reached the location 13 minutes after fire was noticed and began firefighting with foam. Fire was extinguished 15 minutes later and cooling operation was continued for another 15 minutes. OBSERVATIONS/ LAPSES
• The proposal of bypass line was initiated to avoid separator shutdowns during downstream leakage. Management of Change procedure was not followed; modification proposal was sent directly to contract & materials (C&M) department without engineering study or risk assessment.
• The indent for providing the bypass line to the eccentric orifice meter lacked engineering clarity, including line routing, required supports, drain/vent, isolation valve specifications etc.
• Laying and support work of new bypass line was completed 3 days back, but the supports were left with tag weld; final/ continuous weld was not done. No assessment was made to determine whether continuous/ stitch welding was necessary.
• Hot work permit (on hard copy despite availability of e-permit system) was issued on the day of incident to do the final welding of tag welded supports. Work permit was received by welder instead of contract supervisor.
• JSA (Job Safety Assessment) was not carried out, nor the toolbox talk was given to workers prior to the hot work job. Welding work was started without proper booth preparation to contain the sparks and weld spatter. No company employee was nominated to supervise the job.
• Storm water drains contained significant oil residue, even after the incident. Shift personnel routinely flushed lines during sampling, sending oil into drain system that emptied into the open storm water channel. This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents.
• 30 days stock of flammable de-emulsifier chemical (48 HDPE and 93 Mild Steel barrels each containing 180 Kg chemical) was stored near pump house area adjacent to storm water drain without assessment of safe storage capacity and corresponding risks involved.
• As the fire spread through storm water drain and engulfed drum storage area, firewater was applied to douse fire and cool the drums, but the HDPE drums started cracking and bursting releasing more fuel to the fire. Fire water pushed the burning oil towards north-west side, further spreading the fire to cables and instrument junction box area. MS drums remained intact.
• Only three of the eight personnel entering the installation for welding possessed valid MVT (Mines Vocational Training) certificates. CONCLUSION/ ROOT CAUSE
• JSA was not carried out prior to the commencement of welding job. Risk involved with presence of oil in the storm water channel adjacent to hot work location was not perceived. Proper booth to contain sparks and weld spatter was not prepared. Toolbox talk to convey the hazards and precautions was not given to workers.
• Large inventory of flammable chemical stored in process area without risk assessment added more fuel to the fire.
• Lack of training & emergency preparedness; contract workers and company shift employees were unaware of firefighting methods for pool fire and applied water, which resulted in further spreading of fire.
• Failure to follow the Management of Change procedure, absence of engineering assessment, inadequate planning and lack of supervision were the contributing factors to the incident.

context.title: Fire in storm water channel and spreading to nearby areas
context.corrective_actions:
• Management of Change procedure with feasibility study and risk assessment shall be followed for all changes.
• Hot work permit procedure and JSA as per OISD-STD-105 shall be followed for all critical activities involving spark or flame or other sources of ignition.
• Closed sampling system should be provided for all sample points with an objective to avoid/minimize Hydrocarbon draining/ venting to atmosphere.
• Any Oil/ chemical/ water accumulation in storm water drain should be cleared, and proper housekeeping shall always be maintained.
• Large inventory of chemicals shall be stored in dedicated place away from process area with adequate safety measures arrived through hazard identification and risk assessment.
• Emergency preparedness and awareness shall be created through regular mock drills and practical firefighting training for company employees and contract workers. This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents. text: Manual excavation work by the contractor for inspection of underground by-pass lines and mainline valves was going on at SV station. The pit was almost ready to the depth of approx. 2 meters for starting shuttering and shoring activities. During lunch break time at around 14:00 hrs, the security guard on duty heard some screaming sound for help. He immediately rushed to the spot and observed that 03 workers were standing outside the excavation area, one worker was trapped inside the excavated pit up to waist height and another worker was entrapped under the loose soil due to trench wall collapse. Immediately both the entrapped workers were rescued with the help of workers outside and they were taken to the nearby hospital where one of the workers was declared dead. Actual site pictures This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents. Page 1

context.title: Incident during pit excavation work for pipeline inspection
context.what_went_wrong:
• Manual excavation for inspecting the underground bypass lines and mainline valve at SV station has been going on since last 20 days.
• Due to space constraints arising from nearby station piping & PCC, formation of a sloped excavation could not be carried out as specified in OISD standard. Rather excavation with vertical side walls was undertaken.
• The excavated depth to expose the buried mainline valve with stem was approx. 2m. Due to presence of murrom soil, the soil around the buried valve was not found compact. Excavation alongside the PCC area and keeping excavated loose soil on surrounding area may have led to increased pressure on the surface and a gradual decline in soil compactness may have resulted in sudden collapse of trench wall.
• Although the job was executed under a work permit system, the permit classification was not in compliance with company's guidelines and OISD-STD-105. Excavation Work Permit needs to be taken for any type of excavation job and excavation activities exceeding 1.2 m must be conducted under a confined space entry permit; however, only Cold Work Permit was taken for execution of the job.
• The authorized list of permit issuers and receivers was maintained duly approved by the competent authority. On the day of the incident, the issuer and receiver were confirmed to be in compliance with the approval. However, for some days in between issuer and receiver of the permit was same person.
• Continuous supervision by company's officials was found missing.
• Although the job was being carried out under the supervision of the Contractor's supervisor, he was not present at the site at the time of the incident.
• Training records of contract workers covering the job and associated risks & hazards were not available.
• Job procedure for excavation under restricted conditions was not available.
• Job Safety Analysis (JSA) to identify probable hazards and control measures of the activity was not conducted.
• Tool box talk record was also not available.
• Non-compliance to work permit system by not adhering to excavation and confined space entry permit.
• Non-availability of Job specific procedure for excavation.
• Non-compliance to excavation process for depth more than 1.5 m without proper shoring and strutting to prevent cave-in or slides.
• Lack of supervision by official/ contractor supervisor for critical activities involving excavation in restricted area with loose soil beneath PCC.
context.corrective_actions:
• Considering soil conditions, suitable techniques like sloping, benching, shoring or shielding etc. shall be provided to prevent soil collapses during excavation activities. Reference of OISD-GDN-192 should be used in developing safe procedures during excavation.
• Any type of excavation work shall be covered under the Work Permit system. Specific work permit or Composite work permit shall be taken for excavation activities. Further, for excavation more than 1.2 m This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents. Page 2 deep, confined space entry permit shall be taken in line with OISD-STD-105.
• Regular training shall be imparted to O&M personnel on Work Permit System, specifically to authorized permit issuers & receivers. The work permit shall not be issued and received by the same person i.e. a person shall not issue a permit to himself.
• It is mandatory to carry out job location specific Job Safety Analysis (JSA) before issuing the work permit as per clause No. 6.3.1 of OISD-STD-105.
• Job specific tool box talk shall be conducted as per clause No. 6.3.3 of OISD-STD-105.
• Supervision of experienced personnel from Owner / Contractor / Consultant should be ensured keeping in mind the risk factors associated with any job along with their mitigation measures. Critical work should be allowed only in presence of competent supervisor.
• Mainline valve & underground bypass piping should be provided with pits i.e. masonry retaining wall around the valve area inside stations.
• Site specific job procedure/ work practices shall be developed for the safe execution of jobs like excavation as per clause No. 6.1 of OISD-STD-105 and typical requirements to be included in safe work practices as per Annexure-V OISD-STD-105.
• Training and competencies of the contractor workers shall be ensured so that work is executed responsibly and safely as per clause No. 7.4 of OISD-GDN-206.
• The awareness about unsafe act (UA) & unsafe condition (UC) among contract workers shall be enhanced by imparting training to contract workers about UA/UC as per OISD-STD-154. ******* This Safety Alert is based on the Investigation report submitted by industry and published for information purpose only. This information should be evaluated to determine if it is applicable in your operations, to avoid recurrence of such incidents. Page 3

text: The job involved unloading 10 mm rebar bundles from a trailer at a construction site using a 15-ton capacity Farana crane (boom-end hook capacity: 7.6 tons). Each bundle was 12 meters long, weighed approximately 4 tons, and was tied with metal strips at three points. Three fitters were engaged in the unloading operation, excluding the crane operator - two standing on the trailer and one on the ground acting as a signalman. Out of ten bundles, seven were successfully unloaded when the accident occurred while handling the eighth bundle. The metal strip securing the rebar snapped, causing it to loosen and become entangled with other bundles. As the crane attempted to lift the bundle, it was partially placed on the trailer's side wall while corrective action was being taken. A fitter on the trailer attempted to secure the loose rebars by placing a sling around them. However, the bundle suddenly shifted, pushing the fitter off the trailer and rebars fell on him. He was immediately rescued by co-workers, who lifted the bundle using the crane. He was rushed to a nearby civil hospital, however, the worker succumbed to his injuries. Actual site pictures

context.title: Incident during unloading of rebar bundle from trailer.
context.what_went_wrong:
• Although rebar unloading was considered a routine task, no SOP or job-specific procedure was available.
• There was no designated signalman or helper assigned to the crane operator, leading to unsynchronized communication between the fitter (acting as a signalman) and the crane operator.
• The fitters engaged in the unloading activity had limited experience and were approximately 25-26 years old.
• The crane operator was a habitual user of earphones and mobile phones during lifting, loading, and unloading activities.
• The web slings used for lifting the rebars were in poor condition; however, the accident was not caused by sling failure.
• A Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) was available for general loading and unloading activities, but specific hazards related to rebar handling were not identified.
• A work permit was issued to the contractor for multiple activities at the construction site, but it was a generic permit.
• Job Safety Analysis (JSA) was not conducted to identify potential hazards associated with the activity.
• Although generalized toolbox talks were regularly conducted, no job-specific toolbox talk was provided. Although rebar unloading was a regular activity, the accident happened due to
i. Non-availability of Job-specific procedure for the task ii. Failure to carry out risk assessment for snapping of metal strips securing re-bars iii. Untrained workers and casual approach to work iv. Lack of supervision
context.corrective_actions:
• Site-specific job procedures, work practices shall be developed for the safe execution of jobs like handling and lifting rebars as per clause No. 6.1 of OISD-STD-105.
• Job-specific toolbox talks shall be conducted as per clause No. 6.3.3 of OISD-STD-105.
• Training and competencies of contractor workers shall be ensured so that work is executed responsibly and safely as per clause No. 7.4 of OISD-GDN-206.
• Awareness about unsafe acts (UA) and unsafe conditions (UC) among contract workers shall be improved through training as per OISD-STD-154. Reporting of UA/UC by contractor workforce should be encouraged in line with clause No. 7.5.3 of OISD-GDN-206.
• Use of earphones and mobile phones shall be restricted at the construction site.
• All lifting slings, chains, etc., shall be physically checked every time before use.
• Bundling of rebars shall be ensured with sufficiently strong metal strips so that they do not snap during transportation.
• When handling flexible rebars, no worker shall stand within the boom movement area.
• Guide ropes shall be used during lifting activities to prevent unsafe movement.
• Adequacy of Hydra/crane shall be checked before lifting/unloading of rebars. ==============================X===================================

text: A fire broke out on the 1st floor of the under-construction Electrical Sub-Station Building at one of the pipeline sites. The Sub-Station building housed VFD panels, electrical panels, HVAC ducting, insulating material, cabling etc. The fire occurred during a thermal smoke test for the HVAC duct system, using a fogging machine. Thick black smoke engulfed the first floor of the building, which was emanating from the windows and other openings of the building. All workers were immediately evacuated from the building. Immediate firefighting efforts were started by company personnel using water monitors. Subsequently Mutual Aid partners and the State Fire Service personnel joined in firefighting operation. Through coordinated efforts, the incident was successfully brought under control after around one hour. Thermal Fogging Machine Actual site pictures

context.title: Incident during smoke testing of HVAC duct.
context.what_went_wrong:
• Job specific work permit for smoke testing was not obtained. Permit for work at height was issued for the work in under construction building.
• The incident occurred during the HVAC duct leak test using a thermal fogging machine, which works on pulse jet engine technology. The machine operates by using petrol as fuel and diesel is used for generating smoke. However Electrical Smoke Machine with low toxicity smoke fluid was recommended in Job Safety Analysis for carrying out the job.
• The operator performed three smoke tests within ~19 hours (2 tests on day of incident at 09:00 AM, 11:30 AM and 1 test on previous day at 04:00 PM) for identification and rectification of leakage points in duct, with potentially inadequate purging and ventilation between tests.
• During the final test at 11:30 AM, an explosion and rupture occurred in the HVAC duct (at 3 points), leading to ignition of insulation material and spreading dense smoke.
• Safety Management system at site was found inadequate w.r.t. to following: Absence of fire extinguishers o Non-availability of clear work permit documentation, o Lack of supervision. o
• Standard operating procedures (SOPs), Job Safety Analysis and Tool talk records were available. However, the risk of combustible vapours accumulating within the duct system was not adequately addressed in JSA.
• Combustible mixture formation: Unburnt fuel vapours inside the HVAC duct may have created a flammable atmosphere, leading to the fire.
• Inadequate purging: Successive smoke tests with short intervals may have allowed flammable vapours to accumulate, especially in low-lying duct sections near the AHU unit.
• Use of thermal fogging machine: Petrol and diesel-based smoke-generating agents posed an inherent fire hazard in enclosed duct spaces.
• Failure to detect unsafe conditions: The machine operator may not be aware/identified the risk of combustion.
context.corrective_actions:
• Discontinue the use of fuel-based thermal smoke generators and explore alternative testing methods such as optical leak tests, cold-smoke or water-based, non-flammable smoke agents for future HVAC duct testing.
• Training/awareness and competencies of contractor workers shall be ensured so that work is executed safely as per clause No. 7.4 of OISD-GDN-206.
• Ensure the presence of dedicated supervision during high-risk activities.
• Improve fire preparedness by ensuring fire extinguishers are readily available at site.
• Work permits to explicitly mention hazardous activities such as smoke testing with suitable mitigations like LEL testing, extinguisher requirement etc.
• Enhance risk assessment procedures by strengthening existing SOPs and JSA documentation.
• Document and share lessons learned across similar project sites to prevent recurrence. ==============================X===================================
context.potential_consequence: • Combustible mixture formation: Unburnt fuel vapours inside the HVAC duct may have created a flammable atmosphere, leading to the fire.

text: Recently in June 2025, village headman spotted fire and oil spillage along common ROW having two product and one crude pipeline of different companies. The village headman alerted the Line Walker Supervisor, who in turn sent an alert to control room triggering an emergency response action of pipeline operator. Within one minute, pumping operation in mainline and product line of one of the operators was stopped. The central control room, another pipeline operator and DDMA were also informed. The other pipeline operator took shut down of its product pipeline immediately. All MOVs and HOVs on all pipelines were closed within 10 minutes. The State Fire Service doused the fire within 25 minutes duly supported by both pipeline operator's teams. The local Police secured the area immediately, maintained a cordon around the incident area. One villager was reported having minor burn injury. Although both operators halted pumping immediately upon alert, multiple pipelines on the same ROW hindered identification of the leak source. A strong MS odor suggested leakage from product pipeline, prompting one of the operator teams to manually excavate and pinpoint the leak. A post-incident excavation was carried out and found that one ball valve was fitted on one of the product pipelines. A wooden cork fitted on valve bore caused continuous product leakage; also, product was oozing out from the valve welding joint. Ignition was suspected from a discarded cigarette. After carrying out emergency repairs, including split-sleeve welding and static testing, the pipeline was restored within 38 hours of the incident. Subsequently, an FIR was also lodged, and four persons were arrested in this connection. Site Photo showing illegal Valve Fitting Site Photos: Containment & Repair Operations

context.title: Fire Incident due to illegal pilferage attempt on product pipeline.
context.what_went_wrong:
• It was observed that patrolling by line walkers was not effective resulting in failure to detect suspicious activity at the site of incident, which was going on for more than a week.
• Line patrolling was not effectively monitored by pipeline operator and no centralized management system was available to analyze the non-compliance to patrolling schedule.
• No significant pressure drop & alarm from LDS (Leak Detection System) was observed during the incident which are key indicators for such occurrences like pilferage or leak incidents.
• Pipeline intrusion detection system (PIDS) for real time monitoring and detection of third-party activities was not installed in these pipelines, which might have caused deterrence to such illegal activities.
• The operations team of the pipeline operator, in coordination with the state administration, promptly implemented containment measures to prevent public movement near the leak site
• Due to the hazardous nature of excavation near a suspected product line leak, the use of JCB was avoided in the immediate leak zone. Instead, manual excavation was done using workmen with non-sparking tools strictly adhering to safety norms.
• Based on the leads from the investigation, the police have arrested four individuals involved in the illegal valve fitting and the resulting fire. During interrogation, it was revealed that the miscreants have accessed ROW posing as scrap dealers developing scrap yard near ROW.
• Inadequate ROW surveillance by line walkers and ineffective monitoring system by pipeline operator.
• There was a lack of deterrent signage on ROW.
• Effective liaison with villagers along ROW was also found inadequate resulting in lack of information of illegal activities by miscreants near ROW.
• Illegal pilferage created a breach in pipeline integrity which caused MS leakage along the ROW and ignition likely happened by discarded smoking material near the leak point.
context.corrective_actions:
• The line patrolling system is to be enhanced including the following:
a. Effectiveness of line patrolling with GPS tracking system is to be ensured.
b. Centralized surveillance facility to monitor line patrolling activities with GPS device are to be ensured.
c. Changing the patrolling schedule and timings to enhance alertness and effectiveness of line patrolling.
d. Penalty provision including removal from service for repeated offenders.
• Vigil along pipeline ROW and adjoining dwellings are to be increased to identify any suspicious activity. Inputs like movement of loading vehicles/ construction of new house/ facility/ structure near to pipeline ROW are to be collected and investigated.
• In line with clause no. 14.4.2 (d) of OISD-STD-141, in pipeline stretches prone to pilferage a more intense special patrolling plan having electronic surveillance by drone survey and or any other suitable techniques may be explored.
• Villagers / public along the right of way shall be adequately made aware of the possible consequence of hydrocarbon leaks on a regular basis.
• Efficacy of dynamic and static LDS system during pipeline operation and shut down are to be checked at regular intervals.
• To avoid unauthorized intrusion in the ROW, appropriate electronic warning system like Pipeline intrusion detection system should be used for monitoring in line with clause no. 14.4.2 (e) of OISD-STD-141. ===============================X=================================
